Leabhar of Amathaon

Wizard-Protector of the Tuatha de Danaan

A vile pestilence of which I was glad to be rid of was the fell race of beings known commonly as the Boneshavers. Noone knew what they called themselves for they were not the most talkative of creatures. In fact their only recorded contact with others consisted of slaughter and atrocities best left forgotten. The name of their principal city, Yr Coreag, became associated with the darkest nightmares to make even the stoutest of our Riders quail. They practiced the cruelest of sorceries: shadow magic, blood magic and the construction of great structures and artifacts made of bones. It was these obscene structures which gave rise to their apt name ?Boneshavers?. Riders had routed a host of them in battle only to take flight at the sight of what they swore were great pyramids of skulls. Rumours spread and the name stuck.

To this day I am filled with rage and anguish at the memory of the first of their many victims. An oddly mishapen but proud people, known as the Fomorians, who were apparently of Gnomish stock, had the misfortune of residing too close to Yr Coreag. It was not before the Formors were the victims of wholesale slaughter that the other races thought to put down these vermin. To this day one rarely sees a Gnome and one can?t help but feel shame when one ambles by, a lost look upon their face. Finally an alliance of goodly races set out to defeat the Boneshavers, foremost among them were the Danaan. 

By this time the ?Shavers evil and power had grown, fueled by their many victims. Dreadful sorceries were hurled against the alliance, shadow fiends and blood curses smote us, while the Boneshavers used cunning contraptions to crush our troops from afar. A great shadow mage among them, name of Clur'can, was individually responsible for the death of many of my dear comrades.

But the worst was yet to come. One will never know who sought out who; which evil was attracted to the vile corruption of the other ... but sometime during this long and costly war the Grey God himself cast his hand into the fray. Then did we know despair.

(the manuscript ends in a long tear ... leaving the end of this tale a mystery).

Ironhoof speaks. ?We noble Centaurs have long ruled these plains and forests. We hunt the wild antelope that range the sun-blessed fields and feast upon the berries and nuts of the moon-dappled forests. These are our lands, and forever shall be. There have been those who sought to take our lands from us. But they were crushed beneath our hooves and struck down by our blades. We survive while they are food for worms. It is only natural, for we are stronger and smarter than those we have faced.? The old centaur prances about as he speaks and occasionally rears his front hooves into the air.

After a time he calms himself and begins to comb his flanks with a stiff brush. ?But we have not always fought alone. I remember when the Sidhe came to aid us in our time of need. The Shadowgaunt railed against us; giant rat faced creatures with claws that rend your flanks and shred your armour. Fast enough to pull your tail right from you before you could turn and place a hoof in their eye. Proud they were too, they would adorn themselves in the braided tails of our fallen and consided our powdered hooves a delicacy. But eventually they fell to the mighty charge of the Centaur and the deadly bows and magic of the Sidhe.? 

?My great grandsire told me of the hated Boneshavers, a race of such vileness that they made the Shadowgaunt seem quite tame. It is their ruined city that lies to the east along the Barrier river. We hold to tradition and routinely patrol the blighted place, as it is said that one day great evil will once again take root there. In fact we have found and executed several suspicious humans attempting to sneak past our warders and enter the city. You were lucky you had the sense not to cross blades with a centaur or you would have joined them.? He strikes his hooves out rapidly and saunters about, a dangerous look crossing his face.

?But I forget my manners. You clearly are not like these misguided cretins. My scouts have brought word of your battle alongside the Ents and it is clear to me that such noble beings as they would not would suffer the company of knaves. You may therefore have free licence in the Centaur lands - but know that we are always watching and will not hesitate to strike against those who abuse our hospitality.?

Rowan the druid looks tired but pleased to see you. ?Well done my young adventurers. Now that this wasteful battle is over we can concentrate on the true darkness that threatens to engulf this land. On your travels, you might have heard of a vile entity known as 'the Nameless One'. We never mention his true name, for to do so attracts his attention. He is also referred to as the Grey God, for he craves nothing more than total oblivion for this world. Why any mortal would serve a god who only seeks to end all creation is beyond my ken. Perhaps the vilest among us are attracted to his corrupt essence.?

?A century or so ago, a great battle was fought between the peoples that walked these lands before the humans came to settle. Mighty Fir?bolg archers and fell Tuatha de Danaan knights fought alongside centaurs and unicorns against a horde of vile beings known as the Shadowgaunt. The Shadowgaunt worshipped the Grey God and through their blood magic had allowed him to exert great power across the lands. The alliance of goodly creatures put aside their differences and marched to do battle against the Shadowgaunt.?

?The huge and deadly Shadowgaunt cut the alliance to shreds, aided as they were by the magic of the Grey God who at that point walked the earth in an avatar of awesome power. In a desperate act Ossian, the great Bard hero of the Tuatha de Danaan, sang his greatest songspell and caused time to freeze for all living things for miles around him. Tens of thousands of alliance troops sacrified their lives to shield him from the Grey God?s attacks.?

?The battle was so costly that the Fir?bolg and Tuatha de Danaan retreated to their sylvan strongholds in vastly reduced numbers. One rarely even hears tell of them these days. As for centaurs and unicorns I have heard rumour but have not seen one in my lifetime. What I dread is that their sacrifice was is vain ... that the Grey God is still able to exert his influence through the minds of men. His Watch Towers still hold their deadly power, preventing any access to the lands where the Shadowgaunt lived, so clearly his power is not extinguished.?

?This fact was made all too clear to me as something has managed to corrupt some of my novice druids. The majority of them wandered off one night. I now hear awful tales of some forest far to the east where unspeakable rites and perversions of druidic lore are practiced. Perhaps if you encounter this place, you would bring me back more information, as the tales that the trees and animals carry are beyond belief ... you know how animals tend to exaggerate and plantlife has no real sense of time or motion ... but I digress.?

?Know that I have not been idle while you have been out travelling the lands. My druids, what is left of them, have embarked on quests to discover some artificacts and relics which we will have need of in days to come. They have heard word that the mystic Cauldron of Cerredwhen, the great healer, has been discovered. It is rumoured to have the power to resurrect the dead. Further, the Torc of Ossian was seen by some trees to the north. Alas, I have no details on their exact locations but if we were to possess these items, perhaps we could summon the spirit of Ossian himself to guide us in this time of need. He was the only one to face the Grey God and not quail in fear.? 

?Please seek these relics out and return to me.?

Orcish Superstitutions: Rough Draft

In conversation with several Orc 'wise ones' (if that is not indeed a contradiction in terms) I deduced the follow information which might explain their unusual history. 

It seems that several generations ago (the Orcs being almost incapable of keeping track of dates) a religious movement gripped the tribe that is indigenous to this area. The movement centred around the teachings of an individual who called himself 'the Messenger.' He was a skilled orator and soon commanded much respect among the difficult to impress Orcs. The local priests and military leaders attempted to remove him but instead found themselves toppled from power when the common orc soldiers were forced to make a choice. 

The Messenger spoke of the imminent arrival of an entity he called 'the Grey God'. He also referred to it as the 'Nameless One' etc. This god seemed somehow connected to the end of the world as these primitive superstitions always seem to be. Eventually there was a major war fought between the orcs and several other unlikely sounding races on one side and an alliance of races the Orcs call the 'Sidhe'. They pronounce this word as 'shee' which is clearly not of Orc origin. It seems that the Sidhe won this battle.

The wise ones seemed very reluctant to go into details about what happened to this Messenger. The superstitious fools actually seemed quite nervous at his mention. 

In any event the relevance of this brief outline of Orcish history is that at the time of the Messenger's arrival into Orcish society a comet loomed close to the world orb. The comet was clearly visible in the sky for a few days in fact. Records kept in the central Astronomers Guild detail a similar comet in the year 304 of the Rune Blessing which is a few generations ago and could have been the same phenomenon. 

The comet in question was first identified by Nalvari of Kar, that giant among Astronomers, who calculated that the comet was on an orbit that would bring it near the world orb every century or so. 

This same comet, called Nalvari's comet of course, has been spotted by the somewhat shoddy equipment which we have available in this backwater, and is fast approaching. For this reason I shall be keeping a close eye on any strange behaviour among the Orcs. An uprising at this juncture while the Karnak savages remain unpacified would be a grave security risk.

Brachus, Astromer of Tamcaster.

Note: prior to publication remove all negative references to Tamcaster.
